QuestionStmt.S: In hydrogen atom spectrum, when an electron jumps from second excited state to the first excited state, the wavelength of radiation emitted is '$\lambda$'. If the electron jumps from the third excited state to the second orbit, the wavelength of radiation emitted will be $\frac{20\lambda}{x}$. The value of $x$ is

Solution.S:
Using Rydberg formula: $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$.

Case 1: second excited state ($n_2 = 3$) to first excited state ($n_1 = 2$):

$$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{3^2} \right) = R \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9} \right) = R \left( \frac{5}{36} \right)$$

Case 2: third excited state ($n_2 = 4$) to second orbit ($n_1 = 2$):

$$\frac{1}{\lambda_0} = R \left( \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{4^2} \right) = R \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} \right) = R \left( \frac{3}{16} \right)$$

Now take the ratio:

$$\frac{\lambda_0}{\lambda} = \frac{R \left( \frac{5}{36} \right)}{R \left( \frac{3}{16} \right)} = \frac{5}{36} \times \frac{16}{3} = \frac{80}{108} = \frac{20}{27}$$

Thus $\lambda_0 = \frac{20}{27} \lambda$.

Comparing with $\frac{20\lambda}{x}$, we get $x = 27$.

Hence the correct option is B: 27.
